newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends lower, gilts in limelight.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends lower, gilts in limelight.

text.p: Indian call money rates eased further to close at 0.50-1.00 percent on Wednesday, against the day's opening levels of 1.75-2.00 percent, dealers said.
The market witnessed some stray deals at 0.25 percent and 2.25 percent, they said.
The rate may open at 1.0 percent on Thursday due to the lower demand, covered positions and easy money conditions, dealers said.

The redemption of 12 percent government stock of 1997 on June 5 is expected to add 10.0 billion rupees into the system, a dealer with a state-run bank said. "There are no major outflows in this fortnight, while the food credit amount was very low at 1.0 billion rupees today," he said.
The easy call levels will divert interest to the interbank term money market, a dealer said.
The ease in call levels also improved sentiment in the securities market, he said. "The prices of securities rose by 15-25 basis point for short to medium term paper," he added.

The 12.14 percent government stock 2000 saw a major action with a volume of 1.0 billion rupees at levels moving up from 100.30 rupee to 100.45 rupees, against the previous 100.23 rupees, dealers said.

The 12.69 percent 2002 rose to 100.95 rupees, against its previous close of 100.74 rupees, 11.64 percent 2000 to 99.25 rupees from 98.78 rupees, 13.50 percent 1998 to 103.15 from 102.95, while 13.62 percent 1998 rose to 103.86 rupees, compared to its previous close of 103.50 rupees, dealers said.
Yields on treasury bills maturing in April 1998 fell to 9.10 percent from the previous 9.25 percent, the dealers added.
